title: v0.8.1 security-gate mechanical enforcement
problem:
v0.8.0 (released 2026-05-22) introduced the Security Reviewer — the 8th agent — as a coordinated dual-release (Standard 0.7.0 + reference-impl 0.8.0). The 2026-05-25 claw-crypto dogfood validated **the feature's value**: CC-067 caught two genuine bugs the normal Reviewer had passed (an unbounded `float()` parse on a scheduler interval; a leaked `_get_engine()` call per scheduler tick — both fixed in claw-crypto `82e7d94`).

It also surfaced a structural gap. **The modeled `security-review` state was never actually entered**, in any of the four reviewed tasks (CC-067, CC-068, CC-069, CC-072). Evidence, re-verifiable in `~/Workspace/claw-crypto`:

- `grep '"security-review"' .cloverleaf/events/*.json` → 0 matches across all four tasks.
- CC-067's bounce went `review → automated-gates → implementing` — piggybacking on the existing reviewer-bounce edge.
- `security_class` is `null` on every task; the orchestrator's diff-detected writeback never executed.
- Security feedback landed in the reviewer namespace (`CC-067-r1.json`), not in a `-s` slot.
- claw-crypto has no `.cloverleaf/config/security-paths.json` override and `classify-security` never ran — the LLM approximated the entire gate by judgment.

**Root cause.** v0.8.0 specified the bookkeeping in orchestrator prose ("advance status to security-review, then inline the skill"). The LLM driving `/cloverleaf-run` captured the *intent* (run a security review, bounce on findings) but skipped the *mechanics* (advance to a distinct state, persist `security_class`, write a `-s` feedback slot, run the deterministic CLI). Walker history confirms prose-enforcement of bookkeeping is fragile.

The goal is to make the v0.8.0 `security-review` state mechanically unskippable, without dropping the state model the dogfood actually validated. The fix must be both mechanical (the `advance-status` CLI — the only tool through which the LLM moves task state — refuses transitions that would bypass security review for a high-security task) and contractual (the rule is encoded in the Standard's state machine, not buried in reference-impl code, so future implementations inherit the constraint by reading the contract).

The full approved design lives at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-26-security-gate-enforcement-design.md`. A 20-task TDD-style implementation plan is drafted at `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-26-security-gate-enforcement.md`.

**Dogfood lessons embedded** for the Plan agent:
- *Prose-driven bookkeeping is fragile* (v0.8.0 dogfood; walker history at v0.7.x already saw this pattern). Future work that adds new states or new agents should consider mechanical-enforcement up-front.
- *Belt-and-suspenders over guard-only.* Explicit happy-path prose helps the LLM do the right thing; the mechanical layer catches lapses. Both layers earn their keep.
- *Standard patch vs minor.* For purely-additive stricter-conformance changes against a young single-implementation Standard, patch with a clear CHANGELOG note is appropriate — minor is overkill.
solution:
Ship a coordinated dual-release `@cloverleaf/standard@0.7.1` + `@cloverleaf/reference-impl@0.8.1` implementing option **B1** from the 2026-05-26 brainstorm (chosen over B2 CLI-only and B3 merge-gate-only). The full design is the contract at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-26-security-gate-enforcement-design.md`.

**Topology unchanged.** Same nodes, same edges as 0.7.0. The change is preconditions on three existing edges out of `automated-gates`: `→ ui-review`, `→ qa`, `→ merged`. When `security_class === "high"`, these are legal only when `security_review_verdict === "pass"`. The other exits (`→ security-review`, `→ implementing`, `→ escalated`) stay unconditional — so a high task whose verdict isn't pass has only one forward door: `security-review`. The state-machine constraint produces the desired routing without any new explicit "route here" rule.

**Standard 0.7.1 — additive contract pieces only:**
- New optional task field `security_review_verdict: "pass" | "bounce" | "escalate" | null` (default null; reuses the existing feedback-envelope verdict enum).
- `security_gate: true` annotation on the three guarded transitions in `state-machines/task.json`.
- `resets_security_verdict: true` annotation on `review → automated-gates` (rework invalidates a prior security pass — new commits may have introduced new secrets).
- New `validators/security-gate.ts` enforcing the rule against `WorkItem` + `Transition`.
- Conformance tests cover the 2×4 matrix on flagged transitions, a control matrix on non-flagged transitions, the verdict-reset post-condition, the new fixture, and a state-machine schema sanity check (typo detector for the two new annotation keys).
- Standard goes patch (0.7.1) rather than minor with an explicit "stricter conformance" CHANGELOG line — tasks valid under 0.7.0 with `security_class=high` advanced past `automated-gates` without a security review are invalid under 0.7.1.

**Reference-impl 0.8.1 — operational layer:**
- `advance-status` runs `classify-security` at any transition flagged `security_gate: true`. If `declared="low"` and `effective="high"`, it writes back `security_class="high"` and commits before validating. `classify-security` errors fail-toward-review (treat effective as high, warn). If the validator refuses, exit code 2 (distinct from generic CLI error code 1) with a canonical message naming the transition, current values, and the recovery action.
- `advance-status` on a `resets_security_verdict: true` transition atomically writes `security_review_verdict = null` in the same commit (`"cloverleaf: <ID> status review → automated-gates; security_review_verdict → null (rework)"`).
- `cloverleaf-security-review` skill writes the verdict (`pass` / `bounce` / `escalate`) on each terminal branch via a new `set-task-field <repo_root> <TASK-ID> <field> <value>` CLI primitive, in its own commit, *before* advancing status.
- `prompts/security-reviewer.md` adds a top-level `verdict` field to the agent's response envelope contract.
- `skills/cloverleaf-run/SKILL.md` keeps explicit "advance to security-review first when high" happy-path prose (**belt-and-suspenders** — mechanical guard is insurance, not a replacement), removes the now-mechanical prose writeback step, and documents the refusal-and-recover pattern in one sentence.

**No topology change, no agent contract change.** Only `advance-status`, the `cloverleaf-security-review` skill, the orchestrator prose, and the Standard contract pieces shift. Plan, Researcher, Implementer, Documenter, UI Reviewer, QA, and Reviewer agents are untouched.

**Release plan.** Standard 0.7.1 publishes first to npm with tag `v0.7.1-standard`. Reference-impl 0.8.1 follows with `peerDependencies: { "@cloverleaf/standard": "^0.7.1" }` and tag `reference-impl-v0.8.1`. Acceptance scenario (Flow 2, the dogfood reproduction) runs against `scripts/acceptance-walker.sh` before the npm publish step. claw-crypto inherits immediately via the symlinked reference-impl/standard trees; CC-067..072 are terminal and unaffected; in-flight tasks see the verdict-reset fire on their next `review → automated-gates`.
acceptance_criteria: Standard 0.7.1 conformance suite covers the 2×4 matrix on flagged transitions (low×{null,pass,bounce,escalate} all legal; high×{null,bounce,escalate} illegal; high×pass legal), plus a control matrix on non-flagged transitions (all legal regardless of class/verdict), plus the verdict-reset post-condition on `review → automated-gates`, plus the new `task-security-high-verdict-pass.json` fixture, plus a state-machine schema sanity test that recognizes `security_gate` and `resets_security_verdict`.

Reference-impl 0.8.1 unit tests cover: `advance-status` guard refusal (exit code 2, canonical error message) on `high + {null,bounce,escalate}`; allowance on `low + *` and `high + pass`; classify-security writeback when `declared=low` and `diff_detected=true`; classify-security failure → fail-toward-review (effective=high, warning surfaced, guard refuses); verdict reset to null on `review → automated-gates` with commit message matching canonical form; `set-task-field` CLI persistence; idempotent retry on `verdict=pass`.

Reference-impl integration tests cover Flows 1–4 from the spec (clean two-pass, dogfood reproduction, rework reset, blocker → escalated) plus backward-compat for tasks created under 0.8.0 (no `security_review_verdict` field; treated as null; guard refuses guarded advance for high after `review → automated-gates`).

Load-bearing acceptance scenario: Flow 2 (dogfood reproduction) — a low-classified task with a sensitive diff is forced into `security-review` at the door via the mechanical guard. The refusal-and-recover path produces the same audit trail (state events, commits, feedback envelope in `-s` slot) as Flow 1.

Coordinated dual-release ships clean: `@cloverleaf/standard` publishes to npm first with tag `v0.7.1-standard` and an explicit `stricter conformance` CHANGELOG line; `@cloverleaf/reference-impl` follows with `peerDependencies: { "@cloverleaf/standard": "^0.7.1" }` and tag `reference-impl-v0.8.1`. claw-crypto inherits via the symlinked source trees without a per-consumer release.
out_of_scope: Generic `effects: [...]` array on transitions. Two named flags (`security_gate`, `resets_security_verdict`) suffice; promote when a third lifecycle effect appears.
Multi-level security classes (medium / numeric tiers). The `low`/`high` binary stays.
Bypass / skip-security flag. No `--skip-security`. Override is to declare `security_class: low` explicitly (auditable in git).
Per-finding severity routing changes. Mapping stays: `blocker → escalate`, `error|warning → bounce`, `info → pass`.
Aggregate audit dashboard or `cloverleaf-cli security-history`. Data lives in git + `.cloverleaf/`.
Auto-fix / self-healing for security findings. Implementer fixes via the bounce loop.
Cross-task security correlation. No inter-task state.
Telemetry on guard-fire frequency. Git log shows it.
Migration CLI for legacy tasks. Field is optional, defaults null, terminal tasks unaffected.

Changes to Plan, Researcher, Implementer, Documenter, UI Reviewer, QA, or Reviewer agents. Only `advance-status`, the `cloverleaf-security-review` skill, the orchestrator prose, and the Standard contract pieces shift.
claw-crypto's missing `.cloverleaf/config/security-paths.json` override — adoption task flagged in release notes; not cloverleaf code.
